title: Padding, Stride & Output Size
tagline: Move four sliders and watch one floor formula predict a convolution's output size exactly
summary: An input grid wrapped in a dashed border of padded zeros, with a kernel that slides across it at a chosen stride. Sliders for input size W, kernel K, padding P, and stride S drive the animation, and the output grid grows one cell per landing to the size floor((W+2P-K)/S)+1 predicts. One-click buttons snap to same padding (output equals input) and valid padding (P=0), and a live badge names the regime, so the geometry stops being something to memorise.
highlights: See padded zero cells drawn as a distinct dashed border around the real input.
Step or play the kernel across every valid position and watch the output grid fill in.
Read the output size straight off floor((W+2P-K)/S)+1 as you move any of the four sliders.
One click snaps padding to same (output equals input) or valid (P=0), with a live regime badge.
Bump the stride to 2 and watch the output halve, making downsampling by stride concrete.
